rulings.challenge_claim: Two separate challenges. First: the closing curly excerpt for Jer.50.5 is not byte-verbatim against the staged translation and carries no inline web: citation of its own. Second: the row's sole declared driver types the Jer.50.4 temporal opener as a date-formula onset, a family the book's byte-classified date-header object does not contain at this verse, and the twin/recurrence claim binding it to Jer.50.20 crosses two different forms.
rulings.grounds: Both are real and they are DISTINCT defects, not one. (1) Excerpt mechanics: the staged translation at web:Jer.50.5 reads “Come, and join yourselves to Yahweh in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten.”; boundary_rationale renders that run as 'come, and join yourselves to Yahweh in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten', lowercase-initial, so it is not a verbatim substring at exact case (the sole delta is the initial capital). The excerpt also stands with no web: ref inside the verbatim arm's binding window — the field's only web: ref sits far upstream at the Jer.50.4 excerpt — so this run was never bound and never tested; it is one of seven curly excerpts across these eight rows in that condition. (2) Driver typing: the byte-classified date-header object carries 19 candidate sites built on the year-word token plus the bet-plus-cardinal shape, and sorts year-shaped material that is not a date on a per-site read; neither Jer.50.4 nor Jer.50.20 stands among them. Typing an eschatological temporal opener into that family imports tier-1 date-onset seam weight the object does not carry, and observed_substrate_signals is a dependent field of that choice. The recurrence claim compounds it on the bytes: oshb:Jer.50.4 token 2 of 20 reads הָהֵ֜מָּה and oshb:Jer.50.20 token 2 of 20 reads הָהֵם֩ (both byte tier); a skeleton sweep of the four-token opener at Jer.50.4 returns that verse alone (sweep: 1 verse, verse counts, MT keys) while the Jer.50.20 opener returns two (sweep: 2 verses, verse counts, MT keys — Jer.33.15 and Jer.50.20), so the pair is not one recurring form and the second form's other site is never named; no tier label accompanies the claim. The seam itself survives the correction: the turn from Babylon's fall to the children of Israel and Judah is a scene-and-participant change, a tier-1 class in its own right, and the row's own prose already states it. Disclosure verifies: SAMEKH at MT 50:5 (tier-3, single witness), no paseq and no ketiv/qere note anywhere in MT 50:4-50:5. The declared heuristic entry on the pairing sentence is a keyword match on non-exclusive prose and is confirmed a false positive — that disposition does not reach the recurrence-discipline defect, which is a different object.
rulings.remedy: Two orders, span unchanged. (a) boundary_rationale: re-splice the Jer.50.5 excerpt from the staged translation at exact case (“Come, and join yourselves to Yahweh in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten.”) and pair it with an inline web:Jer.50.5 ref adjacent to the excerpt in the same field. (b) Driver swap: replace the date-formula typing in strongest_rejected_alternative with the scene-and-participant change at Jer.50.4, replace the observed_substrate_signals key date_frame.bayamim_hahemah_onset with a narrative_frame.* key, and re-open unit_type and confidence as dependent fields; in device_notes either drop the 'recurs again' / matched-pair sentence or restate it with the two forms named separately, each carrying its own sweep digit, unit and tier, with Jer.33.15 named as the other site of the Jer.50.20 form. Tests the cure must pass — the ones that killed the original: the excerpt must bind to its own ref and match at exact case; the replacement warrant must name a class whose byte-classified site list actually contains this verse; and no surviving recurrence sentence may assert one form across the two sites.

rulings.challenge_claim: The device claim that Jer.50.6 is 'a second doubled ketiv/qere verse' names no swept object and no scope, and against the book-wide inventory it is not the second such verse.
rulings.grounds: The multi-note fact is true and the ordinal is not. The single-witness ketiv/qere inventory records 2 notes at MT 50:6, byte-visible in the verse's own 16-token sequence as an unpointed ketiv at token 3 with its pointed qere at token 4 and an unpointed ketiv at token 9 with its pointed qere at token 10 — exactly the pairing and order the row states, with each ketiv spliced and named beside its qere. The ordinal fails at every scope a row may state. The inventory's multi-note list runs twelve verses in order (MT 3:19, 4:19, 6:25, 13:20, 14:14, 22:23, 48:7, 48:20, 49:39, 50:6, 50:11, 51:34), placing MT 50:6 TENTH at book scope; at chapter scope MT 50:6 is the FIRST multi-note verse in its own chapter, the next being MT 50:11 with 4 notes. The only scope at which 'second' is true is the writer-part scope, which row prose may not name. So the ordinal is unanchored where it stands and false in both scopes it could legitimately assert, and it carries neither a count nor a named object (tier: single-witness inventory, corroborated by the verse's own byte token positions). Nothing else on the row is in question: SAMEKH at MT 50:5 and SAMEKH at MT 50:7 bound the span (tier-3, single witness), no paseq or further note falls inside it, and the two declared heuristic entries are keyword matches on non-exclusive prose, confirmed false positives.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: delete the ordinal 'a second' and restate the fact as a named, digited object — one of the twelve multi-note ketiv/qere verses recorded book-wide (sweep: 12 verses, verse counts, MT keys), single-witness disclosed — or drop the comparative entirely and keep only the two-note statement, which the bytes carry. Test the cure the way the original failed: no surviving ordinal or count in the field may stand without both its swept object and its scope, and no scope narrower than the chapter or the book may be implied.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row places the Jer.50.8 ketiv/qere note on the verse's closing verb while the verse's own bytes put it mid-verse; the ketiv and qere are glossed inside curly double quotes the book reserves for translation text; and at Jer.50.9 the English gloss begins one word earlier than the spliced run.
rulings.grounds: All three sub-claims re-derive from the bytes. (1) Position: MT 50:8 runs 11 whitespace tokens; the unpointed ketiv stands at token 6 with its pointed qere at token 7, and the verse then continues וִהְי֕וּ כְּעַתּוּדִ֖ים לִפְנֵי צֹֽאן (oshb:Jer.50.8, byte tier) at tokens 8-11. The note therefore sits mid-verse, the verse's last verb is token 8, and the verse closes on a noun phrase — so 'the verse's closing verb carries a ketiv/qere note at Jer.50.8' is byte-false, in precisely the verse class where the notes must be read before any position or slicing claim. The substance of the note, a perfect corrected to an imperative, is right; only the location is wrong, and the inventory records exactly 1 note there (single witness). (2) Quote convention: both glosses stand in curly double quotes, which the book-wide convention reserves for translation text carried with an inline web: ref. 'they went out' matches the staged translation at no tier anywhere in this span, and 'go out' differs from the translation's own “Go out of the land of the Chaldeans” (web:Jer.50.8) by its initial capital; neither gloss stands inside the verbatim arm's binding window, so neither was tested. (3) Extent: the Jer.50.9 excerpt is itself verbatim, but its English opens at 'I will stir up' while the paired splice opens at token 4 of 22, leaving token 3 — the first-person pronoun the English 'I' renders — outside the splice, so gloss extent and splice extent do not match. What holds: both splices reach byte tier at their cited refs; the neum formula at MT 50:10 occupies tokens 7-8 of 8 and is genuinely verse-final, so the closure reading in strongest_rejected_alternative is byte-true; and no mark, no paseq and no further note falls in MT 50:8-50:10. The declared heuristic entry is a keyword match on non-exclusive prose, confirmed a false positive.
rulings.remedy: Three orders on boundary_rationale, span unchanged. (a) Replace 'the verse's closing verb carries a ketiv/qere note at Jer.50.8' with a byte-true location — the note stands mid-verse at tokens 6-7 of 11 and the verse's own closing clause carries no note — or splice the ketiv and its qere from source instead of describing their position. (b) Re-set both ketiv/qere glosses in straight quotes; if the translation's own imperative is quoted, quote it at exact case with an inline web:Jer.50.8 ref beside it. (c) Extend the Jer.50.9 splice to open at the first-person pronoun, or re-cut the English gloss to open where the splice opens, so the two extents match. Tests the cure must pass: every located claim in a ketiv/qere verse must be reproducible from that verse's own token sequence, and no curly-quoted run may stand that is not verbatim staged translation text at exact case with its own ref.

rulings.challenge_claim: Converging on one point and diverging on two others: both challenges hold that the cross-reference is placed in the wrong chapter, Jer.49.17 being called this chapter's own Edom oracle; one adds that the closing curly excerpt at Jer.50.13 is not byte-verbatim and lacks its own inline citation; the other adds that a refrain-family substrate key is declared with no sweep behind it, on a two-site framing a sweep refutes at three.
rulings.grounds: The chapter attribution is the SAME defect in both challenges; the excerpt-mechanics point and the refrain-object point are DISTINCT from it and from each other. Chapter attribution: the row's span lies in ch 50 and the astonishment notice it cites stands at Jer.49.17, inside the Edom unit opened by the lamed header at 49:7 and closed before the Damascus header at 49:23 — so 'this chapter's own Edom oracle almost word for word' is false on the row's only cross-row evidence; device_notes cites the verse correctly, confining the error to boundary_rationale. Excerpt mechanics: the staged translation at web:Jer.50.13 reads “Everyone who goes by Babylon will be astonished, and hiss at all her plagues.”; boundary_rationale renders it lowercase-initial, so it is not verbatim at exact case, and it carries no web: ref inside the verbatim arm's binding window, so it was never bound or tested. Refrain object: observed_substrate_signals declares refrain.hiss_at_her_plagues_formula while device_notes states in the same breath that no sweep stands behind it, and the two-site framing is refuted — a skeleton sweep of the two-verb pair יִשֹּׁ֥ם וְיִשְׁרֹ֖ק (oshb:Jer.50.13, byte tier) returns three verses (sweep: 3 verses, verse counts, MT keys — Jer.19.8, Jer.49.17, Jer.50.13), omitting Jer.19.8, while the fuller run carrying the named object and the suffixed noun returns one (sweep: 1 verse). Neither digit, unit nor swept object is given. What verifies: all four ketiv/qere notes at MT 50:11 stand in the bytes in the row's own order, unpointed ketiv with pointed qere at tokens 2-3, 5-6, 10-11 and 14-15 of 16, and the inventory records exactly 4 notes there (single witness); the stated difference from Jer.49.17 is byte-accurate, that verse carrying a prepositional pronoun where MT 50:13 names Babylon, and its suffixed plagues noun lacking the yod carried at MT 50:13 (byte tier at both refs); and no mark, paseq or further note falls in MT 50:11-50:13.
rulings.remedy: Three orders, span unchanged. (a) boundary_rationale: strike 'this chapter's own' — the cited parallel stands in the preceding chapter's Edom unit; keep the reference verse-anchored, with no chapter possessive. (b) boundary_rationale: re-splice the Jer.50.13 excerpt at exact case (“Everyone who goes by Babylon will be astonished, and hiss at all her plagues.”) and pair it with an inline web:Jer.50.13 ref in the same field. (c) device_notes and observed_substrate_signals: either drop the refrain.* key or earn it — name the swept object (the two-verb astonishment-and-hiss pair), give its digit and unit (sweep: 3 verses, verse counts, MT keys), name all three sites, and remove the shared-texture-between-two-sites framing. Tests the cure must pass: every cross-row reference verse-anchored and chapter-true; the excerpt bound to its own ref and case-exact; and the declared recurrence object carrying object, unit and digit together.

rulings.grounds: The staged translation at web:Jer.50.20 opens “In those days, and in that time,”; boundary_rationale renders that run as 'in those days, and in that time', lowercase-initial, so it is not a verbatim substring at exact case, the sole delta again being the initial capital. (b) observed_substrate_signals: drop date_frame.bayamim_hahemah_onset from this row — it mistypes the formula's class and names the wrong form for this verse; the row's declared koh-amar and full-title-stack drivers already carry the seam, so no replacement warrant is needed. rulings.challenge_claim: The opening excerpt splices two non-adjacent parts of Jer.50.21 with an ellipsis and presents them inside one curly quotation as if continuous, silently dropping the middle clause — a verbatim violation.
rulings.grounds: The defect is real but the framing and the severity are both wrong. The verbatim charge is refuted on the bytes: the staged translation at web:Jer.50.21 reads “Go up against the land of Merathaim, even against it, and against the inhabitants of Pekod.” and the row's excerpt reads 'Go up against the land of Merathaim...and against the inhabitants of Pekod' — the elision is MARKED with an explicit ellipsis, not silent, and the operative verbatim standard for translation excerpts in this book is ellipsis-aware: fragments split on the ellipsis must match in order, which these two do, at exact case, against that verse. This excerpt is also bound to an inline web:Jer.50.21 ref in its own field, so unlike the unbound excerpts elsewhere in this run it was actually tested and passed. What is real is the adjacent defect the framing mis-names: gloss extent does not equal splice extent. The paired splice runs tokens 1-8 of 17 and retains עֲלֵ֣ה עָלֶ֔יהָ (oshb:Jer.50.21, byte tier), the very words the English elides, so the Hebrew extent exceeds the English extent it is offered as glossing. Corrected finding: an extent-parity break, not a verbatim break, and severity falls accordingly. The rest of the row verifies: the two further excerpts are verbatim and bound; the splice matches tokens 1-8 exactly; SAMEKH closes MT 50:21 (tier-3, single witness) and the verse carries no paseq and no ketiv/qere note; and the neum sits mid-verse at tokens 12-13 of 17, which the row reports without pressing it as closure.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: bring the two extents into line by one edit at that seam — either cut the Hebrew splice to end before עֲלֵ֣ה עָלֶ֔יהָ so it covers only what the elided English covers, or drop the ellipsis and quote the clause whole from web:Jer.50.21 (“Go up against the land of Merathaim, even against it, and against the inhabitants of Pekod.”) so the English covers what the splice covers. Test the cure by confirming the quoted English and its paired Hebrew run open and close on the same clause. Do not re-file this as a verbatim defect: the excerpt already matches the ellipsis-aware standard at exact case with its own ref.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both challenges name one defect: the row's own terminal verse Jer.50.25 carries the rare prefixed la-adonai plus YHWH-tsevaot title stack, and the row's closing note denies rather than discloses it, deferring the point elsewhere, so a mandated disclosure object in the row's own final verse is withheld and the row gives no positive account of what closes its span.
rulings.grounds: One defect, found independently by both, with the second statement of it the more specific; the extra elements it adds are aggravations of the same defect, not separate ones. oshb:Jer.50.25 runs 16 tokens and tokens 12-14 read לַֽאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת (byte tier) — the prefixed divine-title stack, standing inside the very clause boundary_rationale makes its closing warrant. The prefixed form is its own token object and is invisible to a bare-token sweep: a skeleton sweep returns 2 verses carrying 3 tokens (sweep: 2 verses / 3 tokens, verse counts, MT keys — Jer.46.10, twice in that verse, and Jer.50.25), and the byte-derived divine-name inventory records exactly those two prefixed sites against 13 bare-token sites it never blends with them. So the stated ground — that the clause 'is not cited here as carrying a divine-title stack', with 'a byte re-derivation question on that point is recorded separately' — is refuted by the pointed bytes: nothing about the point is open, and the deferral sentence supplies no substrate grounds for withholding the disclosure (it does not trip the register sweep, so this is a content defect, not a register flag). Two aggravations verify: boundary_rationale flattens the stack to the divine name alone in 'naming the Chaldeans' land as the site of Yahweh's own work', where the staged translation reads “for the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, has a work to do in the land of the Chaldeans” (web:Jer.50.25); and boundary_evidence_refs carries no oshb:Jer.50.25, so the terminal verse is argued without its own Hebrew ref while oshb refs stop at 50:24. Disclosure is asymmetric inside this same stretch, the postpositive stack four verses on and the full stack at MT 50:18 both being disclosed with digits. One correction to the framing of the first challenge: the two prefixed sites share the nations-oracle parent, not the Babylon complex — Jer.46.10 stands in the Egypt oracle, outside Jer.50.1-51.64. The rest of the row holds: the doubled exclamatory particle at oshb:Jer.50.23 and the first-person verb at oshb:Jer.50.24 reach byte tier at their cited refs, the voice-turn at 50:24 is byte-true against the impersonal material at 50:22-23, SAMEKH at MT 50:21 is inventory-true as the front seam (tier-3, single witness), and no mark, paseq or ketiv/qere note falls in MT 50:22-50:25. Uncharged and minor: the Jer.50.24 excerpt carries no web: ref inside the verbatim arm's binding window, though its wording is verbatim.
rulings.remedy: Three orders, span unchanged. (a) device_notes: delete the denial and the deferral sentence and replace them with a positive disclosure — the terminal verse carries the prefixed la-adonai plus YHWH-tsevaot title stack, its own token object, standing at 2 verses / 3 tokens book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, verse counts, MT keys), spliced from source with its oshb:Jer.50.25 ref and its byte tier named. (b) boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Jer.50.25. (c) boundary_rationale: restore the full title to the closing clause's paraphrase in place of the divine name alone, and pair the Jer.50.24 excerpt with an inline web:Jer.50.24 ref. Tests the cure must pass — the ones that killed the original: the disclosure sentence must name the prefixed token object, carry a digit with its unit, and reach byte tier against oshb:Jer.50.25; and no sentence anywhere in the row may report the point as open, as not cited, or as held elsewhere.

rulings.challenge_claim: The clause the row reads as a closing cap is one half of a two-verse doublet whose other half sits inside a fresh onset four verses on, and that byte-true device straddles the row's own back seam undisclosed, arguing continuity for the 50:26-32 stretch against the cut.
rulings.grounds: The repetition is real and undisclosed; the framing overstates what it does. oshb:Jer.50.27 closes on tokens 8-12 of 12, כִּֽי בָ֥א יוֹמָ֖ם עֵ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָֽם, and oshb:Jer.50.31 closes on tokens 8-12 of 12, כִּ֛י בָּ֥א יוֹמְךָ֖ עֵ֥ת פְּקַדְתִּֽיךָ (both byte tier at their refs) — the same construction under different inflection. The digits reproduce but the object needs naming: the two full clauses are NOT byte-identical and each stands at exactly 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse each, verse counts, MT keys); the 2-verse digit belongs to a needle that cuts inside the day-noun token (sweep: 2 verses, verse counts, MT keys — Jer.50.27 and Jer.50.31), and the visitation element alone is common (sweep: 8 verses, verse counts, MT keys), so the discriminating object is a partial-token shape, not a verbatim refrain. The suffixes differ in person and referent, third-person plural of Babylon's bulls at 50:27 against second-person singular of the addressed proud one at 50:31. Nor does the shape straddle THIS row's seam: the second instance sits three verses past it, beyond an intervening row, with SAMEKH at MT 50:27 and SAMEKH at MT 50:30 between them (tier-3, single witness, corroboration only, never a driver). Corrected finding: an undisclosed block-level repetition inside the Babylon complex, owed a disclosure, not a seam-straddling cohesion device arguing against this cut; severity falls accordingly. The row's positive grounds hold on the bytes: the imperative chain at oshb:Jer.50.26 and the bare particle at oshb:Jer.50.27 reach byte tier; the particle's role is split before any digit and matches the byte-derived classification of this site as a woe following the battle call, distinct from the book's woe-oracle onsets, its day-alas, its funeral cries and its sword apostrophe; SAMEKH closes MT 50:27 (single witness); no paseq and no ketiv/qere note falls in MT 50:26-50:27; and all four translation excerpts in this row are verbatim at exact case and bound to inline web: refs.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: disclose the repetition without promoting it to a boundary signal — name the shared construction as the swept object, state that the two clauses are not byte-identical and differ in person and referent, give the digits with their units (sweep: 2 verses for the shared partial-token shape; sweep: 1 verse for each full clause; sweep: 8 verses for the visitation element alone), and splice both closing runs from source with their oshb: refs and byte tier named. Do not restate it as a device straddling this row's seam. Test the cure by confirming the disclosure names its swept object before any digit and that the row's cut warrant is unchanged by it.
